sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Port Container Gantry Cranes and Hoisting Gear

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Bilateral Investment Treaty between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the French Republic on the Reciprocal Encouragement and Protection of Investments, signed 30 May 1984, in force since 1985

Convention between France and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with Respect to Taxes on Income and Capital, signed 10 August 1984, as amended by Protocol of 2 July 2013
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), provisionally applicable to France since 21 September 2017

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L.561-1 et seq. and R.561-1 et seq., as supplemented by Ordinance No. 2016-1635 of 1 December 2016 transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849, and Sapin II Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016; French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Article L.123-11-1 and R.123-1-12 et seq. mandating the declaration of the beneficial owner (bénéficiaire effectif) in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); Decree No. 2017-765 of 3 May 2017 on the beneficial owner register.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport of each individual beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority of the UBO's state of nationality (passport office or consulate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the designated Competent Authority of the issuing state; or Consular Legalization by the French Embassy/Consulate if the state is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Certificate of Good Standing of the direct corporate shareholder, if the shareholder is a legal entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official companies registrar of the jurisdiction of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as required under the jurisdiction of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the Articles of Association and corporate governance documents of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or official corporate registry in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if issued outside France

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (mandat) appointing the French legal representative and the local formation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the place of execution for non-French signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if executed outside France

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, every shareholder, UBO, and legal representative must be screened against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Council Consolidated List of Persons, Groups and Entities Subject to EU Financial Sanctions, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, and the French national list of administrative freezes in accordance with Article L.561-2-1 of the Monetary and Financial Code. PEP status is assessed using the FATF definition, verified through commercial KYC databases (World-Check or Dow Jones) and cross-checked against official national declarations. Enhanced due diligence, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds validation, is mandatory for any PEP, adverse media, sanctions hit, or high-risk jurisdiction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (INPI) — https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; the filing is submitted to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, and the RCS database is publicly searchable via Infogreffe (https://www.infogreffe.fr).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Toubon Law (Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994), corporate registration documents and the company's operating documentation must be in French. The corporate name (dénomination sociale) may contain foreign words only if expressed in Latin script; non-Latin alphabets must be transliterated into Latin characters for RCS indexing. The name must be distinctive under Article L.711-2 of the French Intellectual Property Code, must not infringe prior trademarks, and must be followed by the suffix 'SAS' or the full phrase 'Société par Actions Simplifiée' in all company instruments.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a formal name-reservation window. If the proposed name is rejected by the greffier, the applicant must obtain a written statement of reasons under Article L.123-10 of the Commercial Code. An appeal may be filed as a summary petition (requête) before the President of the Tribunal de Commerce, or the Tribunal Judiciaire for non-commercial undertakings, within one month of refusal in accordance with Article R.123-78 of the Commercial Code. The petition must include the proposed name, the registrar's refusal grounds, evidence of negative company/trademark searches, and written legal submissions demonstrating absence of confusion. No extension of name reservation is possible; the applicant may immediately re-file under a new name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only in the form of a commercial domiciliation agreement (contrat de domiciliation) regulated by Article L.123-11-2 of the Commercial Code, valid for a maximum of five years, with the registered office located either at an authorized domiciliation company, the home of the legal representative, or the company's actual operating site. For ISIC 2816 manufacture of port container gantry cranes and hoisting gear, a virtual-office-only solution is inadequate for customs clearance, CE marking, industrial inspections, employment registration, and documentary trade finance. It is acceptable only during the pre-operational formation phase; a physical industrial establishment must be identified and registered before commercial activity or first VAT return.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% annualized risk for a company with an established industrial plant; 80% annualized risk for a virtual-office-only structure, particularly after the first VAT return, import/export declarations, or customs facilitation request.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified name availability search and clearance opinion (INPI trademark database and Infogreffe RCS screening)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark, fixed fee EUR 230 to 270

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization of corporate documents and UBO passports (up to 4 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent ministries or consular services of the document-issuing states
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing government tariff, EUR 100 to 160 per document, plus agent fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of apostilled documents (estimated 12 pages)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator registered with the Cour d'appel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-page tariff, EUR 25 to 35 per page, market quote for 10 to 15 pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of SAS articles of association (statuts) and pre-incorporation shareholders' decisions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard non-listed SAS with in-kind contributions, EUR 1,400 to 1,800

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration / filing via Guichet unique (INPI) — greffe fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (via INPI Guichet unique)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of approximately EUR 93.80 for an SAS, fixed by ministerial decree

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory legal announcement (avis de constitution) in a Journal d'annonces légales (JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-line / per-column tariff, average EUR 60 to 80

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC and sanctions screening of UBOs and directors using World-Check / Dow Jones
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Third-party KYC data provider / due diligence firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per name screened

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation agreement (domiciliation commerciale) for the first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark, EUR 30 to 45 per month plus processing fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (SAS), L.210-1 et seq., R.210-1 et seq., R.227-1 et seq.; Decree No. 2022-1465 on the electronic sole portal (Guichet Unique); Code de l'environnement L.511-1 et seq. for industrial permits.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Registry) in the judicial district of the registered office, acting through the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Constitution file containing the signed Articles of Association (Statuts), Declaration of Incorporation (Formulaire M0), certificate of blocked capital, registered-office proof, publication notice, and individual declarations; the final instrument is the registration in the RCS evidenced by the Kbis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SAS has no statutory minimum capital; articles fix the capital freely, often EUR 1 for non-regulated activity. In-kind shares must be fully paid on subscription. Cash shares must be paid up to at least 50% of nominal value at subscription and the remaining 50% within five years. Capital is blocked in an escrow/bank account and released only after RCS registration; an attestation de blocage de fonds must be produced.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Pro-Forma First Board Resolution — FR_SAS (English). It is resolved by the incorporator/shareholder that: (1) The company be incorporated as a Société par Actions Simplifiée under the name and registered office stated in the draft Articles; the share capital of [EUR] is subscribed in full and each cash contribution is paid up to the legal minimum of 50%, with the balance payable within five years. (2) The registered office is adopted at the address specified in the Articles. (3) The President (Président) is appointed as sole officer with powers to execute the registration and all regulatory filings. (4) The President is authorized to procure industrial and environmental permits required to manufacture port gantry cranes and hoisting gear and to sign all supporting declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the Articles of Association and corporate governance documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company counsel/notaire (optional); no government approval required at this stage.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Statuts in French containing corporate name, registered office, purpose (manufacture of port gantry cranes and hoisting gear, NACE 28.16), duration (99 years), share capital, modalities of transfer of securities, governance rules and liquidation provisions. Ensure each shareholder signs in person or by private signature; if contributions are made in kind, annex the report of an independent statutory appraiser (commissaire aux apports) and, if a legal guardian or minor is involved, execute additional powers.
required_dossiers: Shareholders' identity documents and KYC data
Registered-office title, lease or domiciliation contract
List of shareholders and subscription statement
Declaration of beneficial owner (if already known)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a defective stipulation is found, execute an avenant (amendment deed) signed by all shareholders and refile it in the dossier; no administrative action is needed before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription and blocked deposit of share capital with a French credit institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (depositary institution).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account under the company name 'en formation'; each cash shareholder transfers the subscribed funds; obtain the statutory certificate attesting the blocking of funds issued by the bank; ensure the certificate contains the exact name of the future company and the deposit amount. On RCS registration the bank releases funds to the company's final account.
required_dossiers: Bank KYC package and shareholder passports
Draft statuts and identity of the company name
Bank certificate of blocking funds (attestation de blocage de fonds)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the attestation lacks required particulars or the bank requests further KYC, apply a cure to the bank by amending the written instruction and obtaining a corrected certificate; any delay should be captured in the formation timetable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal announcement of incorporation in a journal d'annonces légales
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any authorized legal-announcement newspaper (JAL) in the jurisdiction of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and publish the mandatory notice containing the corporate name, legal form, capital, registered-office address, corporate purpose, number of years of duration, denomination and upon incorporation the registration number and the name of the President. Keep the invoice and notarial or publisher's attestation as evidence of publication.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the insertion is rejected due to inconsistencies with the statutes, correct the JAL advertising text and republish; the new attestation is then valid for the incorporation file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the incorporation file to the Guichet Unique (INPI) for RCS registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (INPI) – portal formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; routed to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the official portal, complete the M0 declaration and embedded questionnaires, select legal form SAS and NACE/ISIC activity 28.16, attach the signed statuts, bank certificate, proofs of registered office, JAL publication attestation, identity and beneficial-owner declarations. Pay the fixed state fee online; the portal transmits to the RCS and other public bodies (INSEE, tax and social administrations).
required_dossiers: Identity card/passport of the President and each shareholder
Beneficial Owner Declaration (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
If applicable: statutory appraiser (commissaire aux apports) report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet returns an incompleteness notice, within the deadline use the secured messaging to resubmit the missing item (régularisation); a final refusal can be appealed to the President of the Commercial Court under Article R.123-5 of the Commercial Code.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration, SIREN/SIRET allocation and Kbis issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; INSEE.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After validation, the Greffe enrolls the company under a RCS number, obtains the SIREN/SIRET and a 9-digit auprès INSEE number; the company's status is published in the RCS register and a Kbis extract is issued electronically. Keep the original Kbis as evidence; in parallel open a definitive commercial bank account and obtain a VAT number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a refusal with reasons, submit a written regularisation via the same Guichet; if unresolved, file an expedited request before the President of the Commercial Court to order registration within five days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initial industrial and environmental permit compliance (ICPE and occupational safety)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Préfecture / DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement), with consultations of SDIS and the labor inspectorate (DDETS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before beginning production, classify the plant under the ICPE nomenclature; prepare and submit a declaration or registration dossier (or authorization if thresholds are reached) under Code de l'environnement Articles L.511-1 et seq. Ensure the dossier includes process descriptions, input/output waste flows, accident prevention, and environmental studies. Simultaneously obtain fire safety clearances for the use of welding/cutting, verify overhead cranes and gantry equipment under the Machinery Directive, and schedule periodic checks by an approved body.
required_dossiers: ICPE declaration/dossier (form CERFA depending on regime)
Plant site title and building plans
Waste management plan and hazardous-waste tracking contract
CE declarations of conformity for each lifting machine
Verification contract with an AVEVAP/approved inspection body for the crane
Occupational risk assessment (DUERP) and consignation to the CSE
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DREAL issues a notice or suspend, submit a precision/regularization package addressing each point; contested authorization can be appealed before the administrative court within two months; any 'mise en demeure' must be cured by compliance in the timeframe set.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL); Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours (SDIS) for fire safety; Direction Départementale de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DDETS) for occupational safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: ICPE exploitation approval — Arrêté préfectoral d'autorisation or récépissé d'enregistrement/récépissé de déclaration for the industrial site, together with the CE Machinery Directive conformity declaration for each gantry/overhead crane manufactured and the verification certificate for in-service lifting equipment.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique — Inspection des Installations Classées (DREAL) and Préfet du département.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Conditional classification: for a typical plant assembling, welding and painting port-container gantry cranes, the facility generally falls under ICPE 'enregistrement' (registration) when solvent coating and metal treatment capacity is moderate; if a large painting/powder coating or highly hazardous process is installed, a full 'autorisation' with an environmental impact assessment and danger study is mandatory. Small assembly-only workshops may be within 'déclaration' (notification).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must comply with the applicable arrêté ministériel and prefectoral prescriptions (COD ≤ 300 mg/l, suspended solids ≤ 100 mg/l, nickel/zinc etc. below binding limits), and industrial effluents must not disturb municipal sewage treatment. Atmospheric emissions of volatile organic compounds (VOC) must at all times remain below the limits of the Industrial Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU as transposed in the French environment code; solvent consumption thresholds trigger reduction installations. Hazardous wastes (solvents, oil, paint residues) require a bordereau de suivi des déchets (BSD/ERW) and disposal through validated exutoires; a waste tracking plan and periodic monitoring are obligatory.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Workplace clearance requires compliance with the French Labor Code (Code du travail) on machine safety (Article R.4323-1 et seq.), the 'permis de feu' for welding, and certification of the fixed crane runway's structural compliance (Eurocode 3, EN 1993-6). The SDIS verifies fire resistance of buildings, evacuation routes, gas/solvent storage and the fire water reserve. Occupationally, the site must have a DUERP, a certified emergency plan, and an approved inspection contract for periodic verification (annual) of hoisting gear by an accredited organism (APAVE, DEKRA, etc.).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the official portal impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must submit a formal application to the DGFiP including incorporation documents, proof of economic activity in France, bank details, and business plan to obtain a SIREN/SIRET number and VAT identification number (FR followed by 11 digits). Resident French entities such as SAS are automatically registered upon incorporation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available; limited regimes include micro-entreprise for small-turnover entities and specific holding company tax regimes under French domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: €85,000 annual turnover threshold for mandatory VAT registration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time e-invoicing via the Chorus Pro platform with API integration for fiscal clearance and digital stamping of all invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate applies to exports of goods outside the EU and qualifying intra-EU supplies; requires proof that goods are exported and not consumed in France or the EU
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Penalties up to 80% of evaded VAT plus interest; retrospective clawback for non-substantiated zero-rated exports

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), with prudential supervision undertaken by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR); foreign exchange-control policy and financial sanctions enforcement are co-ordinated with the Direction Générale du Trésor and the French Ministry of Economy, Finance and Recovery.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France, as a eurozone Member State, maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility for the euro under Articles 63-66 TFEU and the French Monetary and Financial Code. No prior central-bank approval is required for the conversion of export proceeds, profit repatriation, dividends, loan repayment, or capital injections to or from the EUR area. Restrictions only arise from EU/OFAC-equivalent financial sanctions, EU restrictive measures, anti-money-laundering screening, and the exercise of foreign-investment screening in strategic sectors (e.g. ports, security, dual-use equipment), which may affect inward direct investment but not ordinary FX conversion. Profit remittance by an SAS is unrestricted provided corporate formalities (audited accounts, tax filings, UBO registers) are current and the payment is processed through a compliant EU banking channel.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender requirement or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts in France. Exporters may hold receivables in EUR or any foreign currency without forced repatriation or sale to the central bank. However, for balance-of-payments statistical purposes, exports of goods must be reported through the customs 'déclaration d'échanges de biens' (DEB) and exports of services through the 'déclaration d'échanges de services' (DES). When a payment transfer between France and a non-resident exceeds the Banque de France statistical threshold (generally EUR 7,500 per transaction), the bank will require a 'déclaration de transfert de fonds' (DTF) to be completed for monetary statistics and sanctions screening. Non-compliance may delay transactions but does not void the underlying commercial agreement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE Group (Banque Populaire / Caisse d'Épargne / Natixis)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for full treasury and trade-finance operations. Authorised EU electronic money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions (e.g. specialist French fintechs) can legally open operational payment accounts for an SAS and provide FX payment services via passporting under PSD2, but they are not credit institutions and cannot: accept deposits from the public, grant loans, issue documentary letters of credit, open confirmed LC/standby LC facilities, or provide authorised FX hedging booking. For an industrial port-equipment exporter with LC-backed settlement needs, a tier-1 bank is required. EMI accounts should be used strictly for low-value operative disbursements (payroll, SaaS subscriptions, minor expenses) and must be segregated from capital escrow balances.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not mandatorily require directors or shareholders to appear physically in the presence of a bank relation officer. Remote onboarding is permitted where the bank applies electronic identification satisfying the ACPR/GNI guidelines and the EU Anti-Money Laundering Directive (AMLD4/AMLD5), including eIDAS-qualified digital signatures and video identity verification with high-confidence document validation. In practice, French tier-1 banks require at least one physical meeting or a notarised/consular certified document pack for non-resident UBOs and complex industrial entities, especially when opening a Capital Escrow Account. The SAS's legal representative must provide certified copies of the statuts, KBIS extract dated within three months, UBO declaration, proof of registered office, and director identity documentation; documents in non-EU languages must be translated by a certified translator.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO identification failure or inconsistent beneficial-ownership register after ultimate shareholder is a foreign intermediate holding company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate-tree chart from ultimate natural person to SAS; audited financial statements of intermediate holding; notarised powers of attorney; RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) extract; sworn declarations from each intermediate director; explanation of source of funds and source of wealth; passport copies and tax residence certificates of all UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high-value trade transactions with sanctioned-adjacent jurisdictions or port counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dual-use/export-licence determination letter; contract and invoice stack; end-user undertakings for gantry cranes and hoisting gear; ICC Incoterms; customs commodity classifications (HS codes); Denied-party screening clearances for all counterparties; corporate register proof of counterparty ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Anticipated capital injection or profit repatriation flows inconsistent with declared business model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital subscription agreement or shareholder resolution; bank-forecasted funding plan; detailed 24-month treasury projection; invoice and purchase orders from port operators; explanation of any lump-sum contribution with validated source of funds; legal counsel opinion on equity vs debt classification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Director is a politically exposed person (PEP) or mirrors PEP flags in the public media
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Reputational and political-exposure due-diligence report; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds memorandum prepared by independent counsel; validated national identity documents; proof of non-conviction and anti-corruption declarations; confirmation of no public-sector procurement involvement relevant to the crane sale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Negative news on port-crane industry, environmental liabilities, or substandard financing allegations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Press clippings with complete context; ISO 9001 / CE / EN 15011 certification copies; product-liability insurance certificate; audited financial statements; prior trade-reference letters from banks and insurers; environmental and health-and-safety compliance certificates for the manufacturing plant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for shareholder loans or equity contributions into the French SAS must use a SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the parent company to the SAS's euro-denominated account at a French tier-1 bank. The remittance information field should indicate 'capital increase / share subscription' or 'shareholder current-account advance' according to the underlying legal act, and the ISO 20022 purpose code should be set to a capital/payment code such as 'CAPC' (Capital Payment) or, where the invoicing purpose applies, 'CORT' (Trade/Credit Settlement) as accepted by the receiving bank. Beneficiary account must be the dedicated Capital Escrow Account if the injection is still subject to legal release conditions. For any single transfer exceeding the Banque de France statistical-declaration threshold (in practice EUR 7,500 and above), the bank will require a completed 'Déclaration de transfert de fonds' (DTF) to accompany the wire; transactions must also pass EU sanctions screening on all counterparties, banks, vessel operators, and intermediate ports.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for the import of components and export of gantry cranes should be cleared through: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct low-value supplier payments; (ii) documentary letters of credit issued by the French issuing bank and advised/confirmed by a correspondent in the buyer's country, transmitted via SWIFT MT700/MT710/MT720, with settlement using MT103/MT202 upon presentation of compliant transport and commercial documents; (iii) standby letters of credit and bank guarantees via MT760 for advance-payment or performance risk; and (iv) euro-denominated high-value payments via TARGET2 or EURO1/STEP2 automated clearing for intra-European counterparties. All outgoing payments must include the correct ISO 20022 purpose code (e.g. 'TRDP' for trade payments, 'SUPP' for supplier payments) and must retain the complete remittance-data set (invoice reference, LC number, Incoterm, contract reference) to satisfy customs-BOP reporting and the receiving bank's KYC monitoring.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD FX forward (plain vanilla, with genuine commercial underlying exposure)
Cross-currency interest rate swap (CCIRS/CCS) on EUR/USD for matched trade-finance repayment
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on non-convertible or low-liquidity emerging-market currencies where the hedge corresponds to an actual port-crane export receivable
European-style EUR/USD currency option purchased for risk containment (premium-paying; no speculative short option positions)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual filing of financial statements and minutes of the General Meeting with the Commercial Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to €10,000 for late filing; potential administrative strike-off proceedings for prolonged delays

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Déclaration de résultat IS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Authorities (Direction Générale des Finances Publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 3 months after financial year-end or 15 May, whichever is earlier
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties of 0.5% per month of tax due; possible interest charges and tax reassessment

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if annual turnover exceeds €800,000 and total assets exceed €400,000 for two consecutive financial years

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual declaration and update of Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) information in the central French tax authority register; updates required upon any change in shareholding or control

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A qualifying small enterprise may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, generally where annual turnover does not exceed EUR 10 million, capital is fully paid up, and at least 75% of the share capital is held by individuals or qualifying entities. Certain dividends received by a French parent may benefit from the participation exemption, generally with a 5% add-back for administrative expenses. Eligible research and development expenditure may qualify for the French research tax credit, generally at 30% of eligible expenditure in metropolitan France up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold, subject to statutory eligibility and documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, with forms 2058-A-SD, 2058-B-SD, 2058-C-SD, 2059-A-SD through 2059-G-SD and applicable sector schedules; mandatory electronic filing through the French tax administration professional portal, impots.gouv.fr, under the EFI or EDI procedure.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with quarterly corporate income tax instalments rather than quarterly income tax returns.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally by the second working day following 1 May for a financial year ending on 31 December. For a non-calendar year, filing is generally due within three months after the financial year-end. The tax balance is generally payable by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end, subject to the applicable filing and payment calendar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN number, registered office, tax office, financial year opening and closing dates, legal form, and accounting currency.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French SAS must report its French legal entity details. Foreign shareholder, parent, or ultimate beneficial owner information does not replace the SAS identification data.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or tax loss, corporate income tax liability, tax credits, withholding tax credits, and payments already made.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the French SAS taxable result after French tax adjustments. Foreign parent-company expenses are deductible only if incurred in the French entity's interest, properly documented, and arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from accounting profit or loss to taxable income, including non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, provisions, depreciation adjustments, and other permanent or temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separately identify cross-border related-party charges, non-deductible interest, mixed-use expenses, penalties, and expenses lacking business purpose or supporting evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year tax loss, carried-forward losses, losses utilized, and remaining losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: French tax losses are generally carried forward without a fixed time limit, but annual utilization is generally capped at EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of current-year taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Loss carryback is generally limited to the immediately preceding year and capped at EUR 1 million.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2058-C-SD, tax credits and foreign tax items
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, foreign tax credits where available, and other tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French SAS may claim only credits legally available to it. Foreign tax credits generally depend on applicable treaty provisions and must be supported by foreign tax certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital composition, shareholding, movements in capital, reserves, dividends, and related equity information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose non-resident shareholders and distributions consistently with corporate records, beneficial ownership information, dividend resolutions, and withholding tax reporting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax instalments, final balance, exceptional contributions where applicable, and electronic payment references.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign parent cannot file or pay in place of the SAS unless duly authorized. The French entity remains responsible for accurate filing, payment, and retention of evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual summary of cross-border transactions with associated enterprises, transfer pricing method, restructuring information, and documentation status, where the statutory thresholds are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose transactions with foreign group companies, including engineering, procurement, management, financing, guarantee, royalty, and commission arrangements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2067-SD, statement of non-deductible general expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certain high-value or specified expenses, including certain management compensation and related general expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Review payments to non-resident directors, executives, consultants, and related parties for deductibility, withholding tax, and beneficial ownership issues.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing may trigger a 10% tax surcharge, increased to 40% for a formal notice not complied with and potentially 80% in cases involving fraudulent maneuvering. Late payment generally attracts a 5% surcharge and late-payment interest at 0.20% per month, subject to statutory exceptions and penalty relief procedures. Inaccurate returns may attract a 40% surcharge for deliberate omission or 80% for fraudulent conduct or abuse of rights.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate income tax instalment and balance payments through the impots.gouv.fr professional portal or approved EDI provider.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly payments; no separate quarterly corporate income tax return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December. The final balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following the financial year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SIREN, tax type, financial year, payment amount, and bank authorization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SAS tax account and an authorized French or SEPA payment method. A foreign parent account may be usable only where accepted by the administration and properly authorized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year corporate income tax liability, current-year instalment base, exemptions, and reductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust instalments for qualifying reductions, credits, or loss positions only where supportable and consistently reflected in the annual return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment generally causes a 5% surcharge and 0.20% monthly late-payment interest. Persistent non-payment may lead to formal recovery, bank-account attachment, public receivables enforcement, director liability proceedings in cases of serious management misconduct, and criminal exposure where fraud is involved.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident recipient, subject to domestic exemptions, European Union rules, tax treaties, beneficial ownership requirements, and anti-abuse rules. Distributions to qualifying EU or EEA parent companies may be exempt under the Parent-Subsidiary regime, generally requiring at least 10% ownership, a minimum holding period or binding commitment to satisfy it, and appropriate legal and anti-abuse conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a current certificate of tax residence from the beneficial recipient and verify treaty eligibility, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose-test provisions where applicable, beneficial ownership, minimum holding, and anti-conduit requirements. Apply the reduced rate only where French administrative procedures permit relief at source or simplified relief. Otherwise withhold at the domestic rate, file the applicable withholding return, pay the tax, and provide the recipient with evidence for a refund or credit claim. Maintain dividend resolutions, ownership records, residence certificates, treaty forms, payment records, and substance evidence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties and similar payments to non-residents are generally subject to a 25% domestic withholding tax, subject to treaty limitation and possible EU Interest and Royalties Directive exemption where statutory ownership, subject-to-tax, holding-period, anti-abuse, and beneficial ownership conditions are satisfied. Ordinary interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to French withholding tax under domestic law, although special regimes and anti-abuse rules may apply. Tax treaties commonly provide a zero or reduced rate for interest and a reduced rate for royalties. Treaty relief must be supported by residence, beneficial ownership, contractual, and substance documentation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 150 million: French entities or French permanent establishments generally within the statutory scope where annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets reach at least EUR 150 million, or where an associated French entity or permanent establishment meets the relevant statutory condition. A local file and master file are generally required for in-scope taxpayers. A simplified annual transfer pricing declaration, Form 2257-SD, generally applies at the EUR 50 million turnover or gross-assets threshold, subject to the statutory related-party transaction conditions. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Substance is assessed through French transfer pricing rules, the arm's-length principle, the general anti-abuse rule, the beneficial ownership doctrine, permanent establishment principles, anti-hybrid rules, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation rules, and tax treaty principal-purpose tests. The SAS should demonstrate real French functions, personnel, premises, decision-making, risk control, assets, commercial purpose, and contemporaneous records proportionate to its overhead-crane manufacturing and project activities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing sales, inflating deductible costs, creating false invoices, misrepresenting transfer prices, concealing foreign accounts, or using sham transactions to reduce French tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, 40% or 80% tax penalties depending on conduct, late-payment interest, and criminal prosecution. Tax fraud may result in up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine, with aggravated cases reaching up to seven years' imprisonment and EUR 3 million, subject to statutory aggravating conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face criminal liability, civil liability for tax debts in cases of fraudulent or seriously negligent management, asset recovery, director disqualification, and seizure. Travel restrictions or imprisonment may arise only under applicable judicial measures and criminal proceedings; the corporate veil is not automatically pierced.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Inadequate Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificially shifting profits through non-arm's-length management fees, procurement charges, royalties, guarantees, financing, commissions, or project margins without functional analysis or evidence of services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustment to arm's-length income, interest limitation or expense denial, transfer pricing penalties, late-payment interest, and penalties for failure to provide statutory documentation. Failure to produce documentation may result in a penalty generally calculated by reference to the reassessed profits, subject to statutory minimums and caps.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur liability where they knowingly approve sham arrangements, conceal records, or organize fraudulent profit diversion. Ordinary transfer pricing disagreement does not by itself create criminal director liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax and Profit Repatriation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, or other French-source income to non-residents without withholding, applying treaty relief without residence or beneficial ownership evidence, or failing to report and remit withheld tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid withholding tax from the French payer, applicable surcharges, late-payment interest, potential denial of treaty relief, and penalties for inaccurate or late returns. The French payer may remain liable even where the non-resident recipient received the gross amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for deliberate or seriously negligent failure to remit tax and criminal liability where non-remittance forms part of a fraudulent scheme.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Beneficial Ownership, and Abuse of Rights
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using conduit entities, circular payments, nominee shareholders, artificial holding structures, or entities lacking personnel, decision-making, commercial purpose, or control over the relevant assets and risks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of exemptions or treaty benefits, recharacterization of payments, tax reassessment, abuse-of-rights penalties potentially reaching 80% of the reassessed tax, interest, and possible criminal fraud proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may face civil recovery, asset seizure, disqualification, and criminal prosecution where they intentionally implement abusive or fraudulent structures. Travel bans and imprisonment require judicial or criminal-law grounds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing, and Sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained project funds, using opaque escrow or payment chains, failing to identify beneficial owners, ignoring sanctions screening, processing suspicious documentary letters of credit, or disguising third-party payments as machinery or engineering invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory sanctions, administrative fines, account blocking, confiscation, contract invalidation, and criminal penalties depending on the underlying offense. Money laundering may carry imprisonment and substantial fines, with aggravated penalties for organized activity or regulated-professional involvement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be personally prosecuted for knowing participation, facilitation, concealment, or deliberate failure to prevent criminal conduct. Assets may be frozen or confiscated, and judicial travel restrictions or imprisonment may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Accounting, Bribery, and Public Procurement Misconduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording fictitious costs, undisclosed commissions, kickbacks, facilitation payments, or improper benefits connected with port, infrastructure, customs, public-sector, or state-owned-enterprise projects.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Accounting restatement, tax reassessment, expense disallowance, corporate fines, procurement exclusion, debarment, confiscation, and criminal penalties for bribery, corruption, forgery, or fraudulent accounting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, executives, intermediaries, and beneficial owners may face imprisonment, personal fines, disqualification from management, civil restitution, confiscation, and judicial restrictions. Corporate indemnification may be unavailable for intentional misconduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Customs, Import VAT, and Intra-Group Goods Misclassification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating customs value, misclassifying gantry-crane components, misstating origin, using incorrect tariff treatment, or deducting import VAT without valid documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of customs duties and import VAT, customs fines, seizure or forfeiture of goods, interest, denial of preferential origin, and possible criminal customs proceedings for intentional evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly exposed under applicable customs and criminal rules where they authorized or knowingly tolerated false declarations. Repeated or organized conduct increases seizure, confiscation, and imprisonment risk.
